title: The King of Al-Yaman and the Night-Blooming Rose

keywords: story of the king of al-yaman and his three sons and the enchanting bird
full_text:
The King of Yemen possessed an exquisite botanical palace, yet his heart longed for the legendary Night-Blooming Rose of Mount Arafat, whose single blossom was said to confer the wisdom of Solomon and perpetual vigor upon whoever smelled it.

He called his three sons and announced:
'Whosoever brings me the Night-Blooming Rose shall receive the royal signet ring and succeed to my crown.'

The two eldest sons set out with fanfare, boasting loudly of their courage. On their way, they encountered a withered hermit sitting beside a dry stone brook, asking for a drop of water.
The elder princes pushed the hermit aside, saying: 'Out of our path, beggar! We ride on a royal quest!'

The youngest prince, Prince Zayd, followed hours later. When he saw the thirsty hermit, he immediately dismounted, offered his leather canteen, and poured water for the old man with gentle hands.
The hermit smiled:
'Prince Zayd, thy courtesy opens the gates that pride locks tight. Mount Arafat is guarded by the Valley of Mirages, where roaring phantom waters drown the arrogant. Take this branch of mountain myrtle. When the mirages rise, cast the branch before thee, and follow the narrow trail of real moss.'

Zayd thanked the hermit and continued into the desert. He soon found the horses of his two elder brothers wandering riderless; both princes had chased the deceptive mirages into quicksand bogs and were trapped up to their chests!
Zayd threw them ropes, pulled them from the mire, and gave them dry cloaks. But instead of showing gratitude, the brothers sulked with bitter shame.

Following the trail of green moss revealed by the myrtle branch, Zayd reached the hidden cliff garden where the Night-Blooming Rose glowed beneath the silver stars like a ruby lamp. He plucked the blossom with reverence and carried it back to Yemen.

When the King inhaled the rose's sweet fragrance, his eyes cleared, his strength returned, and he saw the true character of his sons.
He crowned Zayd King of Yemen, while the elder brothers were appointed to tend the royal orchards, learning that humility and compassionate service are the true roots of noble authority.
moral: Humility and obedience to wise counsel triumph where boastful self-confidence meets ruin.
